primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any trial here is poor -- each is registered and reports its own primary. NOT that the drug or intervention is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. THE CRITICISM IS OF THE POOLING AND OF NOTHING ELSE -- a trial that registers the endpoints it was designed to measure is behaving correctly. The registry is a live document and this reads its contents on the date recorded; a later amendment could change it. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.
primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.
primary.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

pointer_to_another_review_2026_08_21: THIS TOPIC IS NOT POOLABLE AND A DIFFERENT REVIEW ON THE SAME VACCINES IS. Read together without this note the two pages contradict each other, and they do not: they ask different questions. This object asks whether ONE registration, Malaria Vaccine 257049, can be pooled with others against usual care, and the registrations say it cannot -- each trial reports a different outcome. The review at MALARIA_VACCINES_REVIEW.html asks a NARROWER question that CAN be answered: the efficacy of RTS,S/AS01 and of R21/Matrix-M against clinical malaria, each vaccine pooled SEPARATELY and never with the other. It carries pooled estimates for R21 seasonal first 12 months (HR 0.2167, 0.1753 to 0.2678, k=2) and RTS,S recurrent episodes in children (IRR 0.6372, 0.5967 to 0.6805, k=2). A reader who arrives here looking for a malaria vaccine efficacy estimate should read that page. Nothing on this page is withdrawn or corrected by that one.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In children with malaria, does Malaria Vaccine 257049 compared with usual care affect the outcome each trial registered as its primary, which differ across the 3 trials here?

It identifies no trial that can be pooled.

The outcome sought is each trial's own registered primary outcome.

Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21._what: The five reporting claims a PRISMA-2020 manuscript needs that are FETCHABLE rather than argued -- each derived from a field here, or stated as an honest absence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_limbs_this_review_refuses: Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 0 are held (none) and 4 are refused with the obstacle named in the evidence (comparison denominator, grade per pool, model output verbatim, rob per result).
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases: PRIMARY TRIALS. NO BIBLIOGRAPHIC SEARCH FOR PRIMARY TRIALS WAS RUN. The 3 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18. Every seeded registration read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: brief title, registered primary outcome measures, secondary count, and arm groups with types.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.whether_this_review_was_prospectively_re: NO PROSPERO REGISTRATION OR PROTOCOL RECORD IS HELD ON THIS OBJECT. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.
bookkeeping_2026_08_21.that_two_assessors_disagreed_and_where: NO SECOND, INDEPENDENT RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED FOR THIS TOPIC. The judgements were made once. Stated so that single assessment is not mistaken for agreement between two.
